body:
## Status and adopted direction

Target: **Qleisli 0.3.0 type-system specification**.

**User decision, amended 2026-10-02:** retain `Q<Unit>`, but understand it through the general Qleisli type boundary:

```text
T       ordinary/classical value
Q<T>    quantum ownership over T
```

Therefore:

```text
Unit       ordinary singleton value
Q<Unit>    quantum ownership over the one-element basis Unit
```

`Q<Unit>` is **not** evidence that Qleisli needs a parallel classical modality such as `C<Unit>`. It is the smallest and most revealing instance of the generic `T` / `Q<T>` distinction.

The earlier 2026-10-01 decision is retained in substance: `Q<Unit>` remains a distinct linear ownership type; its one-dimensional scalar phase must not be erased; pure introduction/elimination may be specified with independent checking.

Related:
- #196 — three-level surface boundary: `q***`, `Q<T>`, unmarked syntax
- #22 — remove `CBit/CBits`; classical data is unmarked
- #15 — tuple reassociation / monoidal associator
- #18 — owner packaging
- #27 — type-theory synthesis

## Core principle

The monoidal unit should obey the same source-level rule as every other finite type:

```text
Bit        / Q<Bit>
Bits<n>    / Q<Bits<n>>
Unit       / Q<Unit>
```

There is no third source-level “basis Unit” and no need for `C<Unit>`.

The role of `Unit` changes only by context:

- as an ordinary type, it contains the ordinary value `()`;
- under `Q<Unit>`, the same singleton basis generates a one-dimensional quantum space.

This is the unit case of the general interpretation:

```text
A        ordinary finite value space
Q<A>     linear quantum ownership with computational basis A
```

## Why `Q<Unit>` still matters

Although `Unit` has only one value, `Q<Unit>` cannot simply be replaced by ordinary `Unit`.

The empty wire list denotes a **one-dimensional**, not zero-dimensional, Hilbert space:

```text
H(Unit) = ℂ
```

A unitary on it may carry a scalar phase:

```text
Uθ |()> = exp(iθ) |()>
```

That phase becomes observable under coherent control:

```text
Uπ = [-1]
controlled(Uπ) = diag(1, -1) = Z
```

Therefore:

> **zero physical wires does not imply zero quantum semantics.**

This is exactly why the generic `Q<T>` distinction remains meaningful even at `T = Unit`.

## Ownership interpretation

`Q<Unit>` remains a linear owner in the source/core ownership discipline.

This is primarily a **uniform semantic and verification rule**, not a no-cloning necessity for a singleton state:

- every `Q<A>` participates in the same move/consume/return accounting;
- zero-width owners cannot disappear merely because their physical wire count is zero;
- operations on them may retain scalar phase;
- controlled composition may expose that phase;
- evidence and interface identity must not silently change when an empty owner is removed.

Thus the generic rule is preserved without inventing a special “classical unit modality”.

## Monoidal unit coherence

The tensor unit has canonical isomorphisms:

```text
A ⊗ Unit ≅ A ≅ Unit ⊗ A
```

These are canonical structure maps, but need not be definitional type equalities in the verified core.

The surface/elaborator may eventually strictify canonical unit structure where #15/#18 permit it, provided:

- leaf/axis order is unchanged;
- the inserted map has exact phase +1;
- ownership is preserved;
- the core independently checks the resulting explicit structure;
- scalar operations on a `Q<Unit>` factor are never erased by structural simplification.

In particular, “remove the Unit factor” and “erase all Unit-only quantum computation” are **not** the same transformation.

## Pure introduction and elimination

Retain the 2026-10-01 direction that Qleisli may specify explicit pure structure maps, with names still illustrative:

```text
unit   : Unit    -> Q<Unit>
finish : Q<Unit> -> Unit
```

Their canonical structural meaning is phase +1.

Conceptually:

```text
η(1) = |()>
ε(|()>) = 1

ε ∘ η = id_ℂ
η ∘ ε = id_H(Unit)
```

They allocate/consume a logical zero-width owner without measurement, reset or partial trace.

Crucially, elimination is **not phase normalization**:

```text
ε ∘ Uθ ∘ η = exp(iθ) id_ℂ
```

So a computation returning ordinary `()` may still carry a nontrivial scalar operator in its checked quantum meaning.

The final public spelling of these maps remains open; the semantic requirement does not depend on the names `unit` and `finish`.

## Relation to observation

Do not confuse:

```text
Q<Unit> -> Unit
```

pure structural elimination with general observation:

```text
Q<A> -> A
```

The latter is not a generic coercion and is not permitted merely because #22 removes the `C` prefix.

For nontrivial `A`, obtaining an ordinary value requires an explicit operation with appropriate `Observe` semantics.

The unit case is special only because its Hilbert space is canonically one-dimensional; it does **not** establish a generic `Q<T> -> T` conversion.

## Relation to #22

#22 now adopts:

```text
Bit       ordinary
Q<Bit>    quantum-owned

Bits<n>   ordinary
Q<Bits<n>> quantum-owned
```

This issue must match exactly:

```text
Unit      ordinary
Q<Unit>   quantum-owned
```

The consistency requirement is more important than any particular API spelling.

This eliminates the old temptation to describe classical terminal data, basis Unit and quantum unit as three separate source-level type universes.

## `Bits<0>` question

`Bits<0>` is also a singleton finite type.

0.3.0 still needs to decide whether:

```text
Bits<0> = Unit
```

definitionally at the surface, or whether they are distinct finite types connected by a canonical map.

Whichever choice is made:

- `Q<Bits<0>>` and `Q<Unit>` must preserve any scalar phase semantics;
- equal physical width alone must not authorize arbitrary receipt/evidence substitution;
- no optimization may erase a controlled scalar merely because both representations use zero physical wires.

## Lowering and verification obligations

- Preserve linear moves for `Q<Unit>`; reject duplicate, omitted and revived zero-width owners.
- Preserve scalar phase exactly through adjoint, repetition, tensoring and coherent control.
- Keep ordinary `Unit` unrestricted as ordinary data.
- Do not introduce `C<Unit>`.
- Distinguish source-level coherence convenience from core evidence/type identity.
- Runtime handle erasure must preserve source/evidence binding and the accepted operator meaning.
- Resource accounting assigns zero physical qubits to `Q<Unit>`, while checker/evidence representation may still consume compile-time resources.
- Pure removal of a zero-width owner must not authorize release of nontrivial ancillas such as `Q<Bit>`; those retain their own cleanup/separation obligations.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The Language Reference presents `Unit` / `Q<Unit>` as the unit instance of the generic `T` / `Q<T>` boundary.
2. No source-level `C<Unit>` or separate “classical Unit type” is introduced.
3. `H(Unit)=ℂ` and phase-bearing zero-wire operations are specified explicitly.
4. Controlled scalar-phase regressions remain valid, including `[-1]` becoming a nontrivial controlled phase.
5. Pure introduction/elimination, if exposed, preserve phase and are independently checked.
6. Canonical left/right unitors have phase +1 and preserve surrounding/reference state.
7. Structural simplification cannot erase a nontrivial scalar operator on a `Q<Unit>` factor.
8. `Bits<0>` / `Unit` equality-or-coherence is decided explicitly.
9. Zero-width owners remain covered by ownership/evidence tests even though they use zero physical qubits.
10. The final specification is consistent with #22 and #196 without creating a second classical modality.

## Design principle

> **`Unit` is ordinary because ordinary is the default. `Q<Unit>` is quantum because `Q` is the modality.**

And:

> **Zero wires is not zero meaning.**

This is the minimal case that tests whether the `T` / `Q<T>` boundary is semantically honest.

## 2026-10-04 target type contract

Keep `Unit` and `Bits<0>` definitionally distinct in 0.3.0. Both owned forms retain linear accounting and scalar phase. A pure introduction/elimination rule must be explicit and checked; no ordinary Unit coercion erases the quantum owner. This conservative current contract does not bring #197's future implicit conveniences forward.

The [target Language Reference](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/reference/type-model.md) and [foundation analysis](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/design/type-foundation.md) record this ordinary implementation decision under the approved 0.3.0 plan and adopted authority hierarchy. Edition remains 2026. This is not a new Guardian interpretation or guarantee admission.

Status: target rules selected; implementation and conformance remain in progress in #307. Current alpha syntax still contains CBit/CBits and general Basis polymorphism is not yet implemented. Required positive and negative tests, exact lowering/interface preservation and native acceptance evidence remain open. Documentation alone does not complete this issue.
title: 0.3.0: define `Unit` / `Q<Unit>` under the `T` vs `Q<T>` boundary
